- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 3% from prior peak), model frequently overestimates continuation; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, reducing forecast slope by 20–40% for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment change by 10–20% in the 2–5 day window.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 3σ from 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversion; if below, increase by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating volatility in high-sentiment periods; reduce forecast variance by 15–25% when sentiment > 0.7 for 5+ consecutive days.
